name: Orders
descr: The orders of the shop. An order is never changed in place: every change is a new version of it, and the version the order stands at now is the one the shop shows. CmdQuery finds and reads orders whole. The work on one order walks in a circle: CmdLoad answers its version as one array - or CmdCreate answers a blank one - the array is shaped in your hands or by the goods and option commands, CmdCalc counts the money the way the shop counts it, and CmdEdit saves the array as the new version of the order. Every step of the circle passes through the very logic the storefront checkout runs - the discounts, the option sums, the refusals of the shop included - and never straight into the tables. The right to see an order goes by the values of its options, a status among them; saving takes the ORDER_VERSION_ADD operation of the store.

commands.name: CmdQuery
commands.descr:
Finds the orders by a query written as json and answers each of them whole - the head with its code, the current version, the goods in it, the options of the order, the options standing on every goods, and the fields the buyer filled.

ASKED FOR NOTHING - an empty query, or none at all - it answers its own signature instead: every table with every column and its type, and what may be asked of each. Nothing outside that list is taken, so a first call asks for it and the ones after are built by it.

THE SHAPE. A query starts from the root table of the sign and holds a list of conditions. A list is an AND, always. Four things may stand in it:
a condition - {"field": "code", "op": "like", "value": "781"};
an or - {"or": [ ..., ... ]};
a not - {"not": ...}, of one condition or of one nested table;
a nested table - {"orders_option": [ ... ]}, which means THERE IS such a row: every condition inside it holds on one and the same row. A table goes one level deep only, and only a table the sign marks nest.

ONE VERSION OF ONE ORDER. The root is the order itself - its id, its code, the day it was made. Everything else nests, and every nested table stands on the version the order is at now, so an order is one row and never many; the versions it stood at before are not reached from here. The money and the buyer of the order are orders_version: {"orders_version": [{"field": "total_sum", "op": "ge", "value": 1000}]}.

THE STATUS AND EVERY OTHER OPTION is a row of orders_option, and the key of a value is what to look by: {"orders_option": [{"field": "option_skey", "op": "eq", "value": "status"}, {"field": "value_skey", "op": "eq", "value": "new"}]}. Both conditions hold on one row, which is what makes it the status and not any option that happens to carry that value.

THE BUYER is asked for the same way, by his fields: {"orders_client_field": [{"field": "field_skey", "op": "eq", "value": "phone"}, {"field": "value_txt", "op": "like", "value": "380 67"}]}. The keys of the fields and of the options are the ones the shop was set up with - a first answer of any order shows them all.

THE GOODS of an order are a nested table too: {"orders_store": [{"field": "store_id", "op": "in", "value": [25, 26]}]} finds the orders one of those goods was bought in. The row keeps the goods as it was then - its name, its codes, its price - so an order reads the same after the goods itself has changed or gone.

NOTHING STANDS BESIDE THE ROOT TABLE. The page is a field of the call - limit and offset - and the orders come by id, page after page, so a walk of many pages loses none and says none twice. Whatever the page, the answer carries found - the whole count of what matched.

THE OPERATIONS come from the type of the column, and the sign names them: eq, in, between, ge, le for numbers, eq, between, ge, le for days, eq, in, like for words, eq for flags.

AN EXAMPLE of the whole thing:
{"orders": [
  {"field": "date_time", "op": "ge", "value": "2026-08-01"},
  {"orders_version": [ {"field": "total_sum", "op": "ge", "value": 1000} ]},
  {"orders_option": [ {"field": "option_skey", "op": "eq", "value": "status"},
                      {"field": "value_skey", "op": "in", "value": ["new", "work"]} ]},
  {"not": {"orders_option": [ {"field": "option_skey", "op": "eq", "value": "delivery"},
                              {"field": "value_skey", "op": "eq", "value": "pickup"} ]}}
]}

params.name: query
params.descr: the query itself, as the shape above; left out or empty, the command answers what may be named in one

params.name: limit
params.descr: how many orders of the ones found to answer with; found says how many there are in all, so a page is chosen knowing the size

params.name: offset
params.descr: how many of the orders found to step over before this page - 100 takes the second page of a hundred

commands.name: CmdCreate
commands.descr: Answers a blank version of a new order: the buyer fields of the shop empty, the order options at their defaults, no goods. Shape it and save with CmdEdit - the order and its buyer are born there. The array is the same one CmdLoad answers, so the circle of the commands is one whatever the order began as.

commands.name: CmdLoad
commands.descr: Answers the version the order stands at now as one array: the head fields with parent_version_id - the version this array grew from; client - the buyer fields with their values; store - the goods rows, each carrying its snapshot of the goods and its store_option list; option - the order options with the sums they add. Change the array yourself or hand it to the commands; parent_version_id is what CmdEdit weighs the order by, so an array held too long meets VERSION_ERROR there and is loaded afresh.

params.name: order_id
params.descr: the order to load; CmdQuery finds the ids

commands.name: CmdGoodsAdd
commands.descr: Puts a goods into the version: reads it from the shop as it is now - the prices brought to the shop currency, the codes, the name - hangs the goods options of the shop on it at their defaults, and answers the version grown by that row. A goods already in the version grows its amount instead. The base itself is untouched until CmdEdit.

params.name: version
params.descr: the order array, as CmdLoad or CmdCreate answered it

params.name: store_id
params.descr: the goods to put in, by its id in the shop

params.name: amount
params.descr: how many of it; a goods already in the version grows by this

params.name: price_out
params.descr: the selling price to stand on the row; the calculation overwrites it while the row asks to be counted - hold your own by setting recalc to 0 on the row

commands.name: CmdGoodsRemove
commands.descr: Takes a goods out of the version and answers what is left; a goods the version does not hold is refused by name. The base itself is untouched until CmdEdit.

params.name: version
params.descr: the order array, as CmdLoad or CmdCreate answered it

params.name: store_id
params.descr: the goods to take out, by its id in the shop

commands.name: CmdOptionSet
commands.descr: Sets an order option by the keys of the registry: the names, the sum and the money words of the value come along by themselves. An unknown key is refused with the list of what the shop holds. The base itself is untouched until CmdEdit.

params.name: version
params.descr: the order array, as CmdLoad or CmdCreate answered it

params.name: option
params.descr: the skey of the order option

params.name: value
params.descr: the skey of its value; a free-input option takes none - write value_name into the array itself

params.name: notice
params.descr: the word onto the option row; it takes the place of what stands there unless keep is said

params.name: keep
params.descr: true - the notice standing on the option row is left as it is and notice is not read at all; false - the notice given takes its place

commands.name: CmdCalc
commands.descr: Counts the version the way the shop counts an order - the discounts of the goods, then the option sums in their order - and answers the version with total_sum set. What the shop refuses to take - a blocked pair of values, an option not yours to change - comes back as the refusal it would meet at saving. Nothing is written; run it before CmdEdit to see the money and the refusals early.

params.name: version
params.descr: the order array, as CmdLoad or CmdCreate answered it

commands.name: CmdEdit
commands.descr: Saves the version as the new version of its order - or births the order and its buyer when order_id is empty - and answers the order id. The shop verifies before it writes: the blocked pairs, the option rights, the limits; and an array grown from a version the order no longer stands at is refused as VERSION_ERROR - load it afresh and carry the change over. This is the only command of the circle that writes.

params.name: version
params.descr: the order array to save; its parent_version_id must be the version the order stands at, or the answer is VERSION_ERROR
